title: Staggered kernel onboarding and regret-metering for v2/v3 FlashAttention mix
creator: Aisha Delgado
description: Background: We have observed intermittent latency variance and rare token-level regressions when switching between FlashAttention v2 and v3 kernels on long-context decode heavy workloads. This ticket introduces a staggered onboarding mechanism that gradually enrolls model requests onto the v3 kernel while continuously measuring a regret metric that captures quality deltas and tail-latency impact. Goal: Enable safe, measurable rollout of v3 kernels with automated rollback when regret exceeds thresholds. Deliverables: 1) staged enrollment controller (staggered percent + heat-up window), 2) regret-meter telemetry (per-route token delta + semantic regression sampler), 3) fast rollback trigger and canary dashboard, 4) documentation and runbook for on-call. Success metrics: reduced regression incidents to <=1 per 100k requests for enrolled routes, maintain 99th latency within 5% of baseline, and no increase in customer-visible error rates.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Staggered controller deployed in canary; supports policies: linear ramp, sigmoid ramp, and manual step. 2) Regret-meter emits per-model/per-route daily aggregate and alert when semantic-regret > 0.5 or token-LL drop > 1.0 across sample. 3) Automated rollback triggers and verified on staging; PRs merged with unit + integration tests. 4) Runbook updated and reviewed by SRE and ML research.
technical_notes: Design sketch: on enrollment request, runtime picks candidate kernel based on policy percent. A lightweight sampler duplicates a small fraction (~0.5%) of requests for offline comparison using v2/v3 outputs. Regret metric is a composite: token-level log-likelihood delta (LL_delta), deterministic structural diffs (JSON path mismatches for structured outputs), and a semantic similarity score (embedding cosine on sampled responses). Storage: sampler payloads write to a bounded ring buffer topic (kafka://attn-regret-samples) for downstream offline eval. Safety: duplicate sampling is async and must not affect p99 latency; fallback path returns first-completed response. Rollback logic: if rolling-window regret > threshold for 30min and sample volume >= 200, flip route to last-stable kernel and notify SOC. Performance: bundled kernel needs light-weight handshake to check workspace availability; prefer micro-batch alignment to avoid thrashing.
testing_plan: Unit tests for controller logic and config parsing. Integration: run mixed-kernel decoding harness in CI with synthetic long-context traces (varying sequence lengths up to 64k tokens). End-to-end: deploy to staging with 5% of internal traffic, enable sampler, validate against regression detector and stress test with burst traffic. Load tests: scale until p95 latency crosses slos to validate safety margins. Chaos test: simulate kernel OOM and verify rollback and buffer recovery.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: feature flag behind runtime gate (internal only). Phase 1: Canary to internal non-prod routes (5%). Phase 2: Canary to internal prod routes (20%) with regret sampling on. Phase 3: Gradual ramp to 50% using linear schedule if regret < threshold for 72h. Phase 4: Full ramp to 100% for compatible routes and formal deprecation of v2 where appropriate. Each phase requires a go/no-go checklist: telemetry healthy, no regression alerts, SLOs met. Manual override available via console toggle and API.
telemetry_queries: bigquery:regret_sampler.samples_table: SELECT route, LL_delta, semantic_sim FROM samples WHERE ts > TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 1 DAY)
qa_steps: Enable feature flag in staging and confirm controller respects percent policy
Verify sampler writes to kafka with correct schema and bounded size
Run offline comparator on sampled pairs and confirm regret metric calculation matches spec
Inject synthetic semantic regressions to ensure alerting fires
Exercise rollback path and confirm route flips and alerts are sent
